analysis.title: Morgan Stanley's 2027 Outlook: "Embracing Risk"
key_insights: Morgan Stanley takes a broadly positive stance on risk for 2027, citing an AI capex cycle it views as intact, a resilient global economy, solid earnings growth extending into 2027, major risk catalysts behind us, and risk assets that have cheapened over the past six months.
Economists see a resilient global economy facing a harder inflation backdrop. Growth modestly exceeded mid-year expectations, led by US strength and an investment cycle broadening globally.

Global growth is expected to soften modestly in 2027 and return to its 2026 pace in 2028 as energy headwinds recede. The expected brief tightening cycle assumes that relief materializes, and persistent inflation is the key risk.

Energy is the principal complication. Wide spreads between crude and refined products and regional differences in delivered prices mean crude alone understates the inflation signal. Energy, food and supply-chain costs could feed into core inflation and prompt tighter policy even where growth is vulnerable, particularly in emerging markets.

Regional drivers differ. The US remains the main engine on AI infrastructure investment and consumer spending supported by wealth and full employment. German fiscal support and periphery growth underpin Europe's moderate expansion. China's growth is modest as the deflationary cycle fades. Industrial investment is broadening across Asia.
Equity analysts have kept their baseline AI capex projections despite policy uncertainty after the US midterm elections.

Strategists are constructive on global equities on continued strong earnings growth. Elevated funding costs and record borrowing needs call for a quality bias: strong balance sheets, durable margins and cash generation. The expected shift toward cyclicals is a rotation within quality.
In credit, Morgan Stanley raises US investment grade to equal weight, cuts high yield to underweight, and moves up in quality within hard-currency EM sovereigns and securitized credit.

Credit markets are expected to play a larger role in funding AI capex in 2027. High-quality issuers keep access to multiple financing channels, while lower-rated participants rely more on asset-backed financing, often supported by higher-rated counterparties.

Allocation: maximum overweight in global equities and a neutral allocation to US Treasuries, keeping duration because equity exposure is high. The firm says tail risks still strengthen the case for portfolio protection.
The firm expects fewer macro shocks in its base case but more weight on shifts beneath the surface, with focus on evidence of returns to AI capex in hyperscaler earnings and broader AI adoption.

Cut to underweight as part of a preference for quality across credit.
Duration is kept because equity exposure is high.
The expected shift toward cyclicals is described as a rotation within quality.

earnings_insights: Morgan Stanley expects solid earnings growth to extend into 2027, with no specific EPS or revenue figures given.

macro_indicators.reading: Expected to soften modestly in 2027, then return to the 2026 pace in 2028
macro_indicators.interpretation: Energy headwinds are expected to recede by end-2027, supporting the 2028 rebound.
The forecast assumes energy relief materializes. Persistent inflation is the key risk to it.

risk_factors: Persistent inflation from energy, food and supply-chain pressures feeding into core inflation.
Tighter policy in economies where growth is vulnerable, particularly emerging markets.
Weak evidence of returns to AI capex in hyperscaler earnings and broader AI adoption.
Elevated funding costs and record borrowing needs, especially for lower-rated issuers.
Policy uncertainty after the US midterm elections.
vol_and_positioning: Morgan Stanley says uncertainty and tail risks remain significant, which strengthens the case for portfolio protection alongside a maximum overweight in global equities.
geopolitical: Geopolitical shocks in 2026 reshaped the global economy and monetary policy.
Policy uncertainty after the US midterm elections.

tension_points.bull_case: Energy headwinds recede by end-2027, so only a brief tightening cycle is needed and global growth returns to its 2026 pace in 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy, food and supply-chain costs feed into core inflation, prompting tighter policy even where growth is vulnerable, particularly in emerging markets. This is the firm's downside scenario.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy relief failing to materialize by end-2027.
